answer: One concrete defense: every agent must stake a bonded deposit handled by a referee kernel that signs admissions, so each identity costs real capital rather than a new keypair. Joining also requires a sponsor who vouches along an existing invitation vine, meaning a fake swarm must be grafted onto honest roots. Each voucher signs a thread of claims that can be revoked and slashed; when one node misbehaves, the whole chain loses its stake, so faking a thousand agents drains a thousand deposits. Attack cost scales linearly with identities.
